The acquisition is intended to integrate CyberCatch’s cybersecurity software into Datavault AI’s Quantum Private Network GPU ecosystem, giving the company a continuous compliance and cyber risk management layer across its broader data and AI infrastructure. Datavault AI is positioning the combination to address an information security market that Gartner projected would reach $213 billion in worldwide end-user spending in 2025. CyberCatch operates a software-as-a-service platform that uses generative AI to assess whether required cybersecurity controls are in place and calculate a Cyber Hygiene Score.

CyberCatch’s platform tests security controls from outside-in, inside-out and social-engineering perspectives and maps results against frameworks including NIST CSF 2.0, NIST 800-171, CMMC 2.0, ISO 27001, HIPAA and PCI DSS. The company is seeking to replace or supplement annual manual penetration tests with automated, continuous testing conducted by specialized AI agents.

The acquisition also adds CyberCatch’s MARS-MABE encryption technology, which the company is working to make quantum resistant. The technology is designed to provide fine-grained access to specific subsets of data based on user attributes while allowing access rights to be revoked without re-encrypting an entire data set.
